name: ahuarte47/duckdb-eurostat
what_it_holds: DuckDB extension (35 stars, MIT, updated 9 Sep 2026) that exposes the Eurostat database as SQL tables directly inside DuckDB, so any Eurostat dataset (including tour_ce_omr and related tourism/accommodation tables) can be queried with plain SQL.
why_useful: Repo's own environment already uses DuckDB for large-store queries; this extension would let the team pull/refresh Eurostat platform-tourism tables in the same DuckDB workflow used for Inside Airbnb, with no separate Python/R dependency.
duplicate_of_holding: same Eurostat tables already held via other means
size_hint: extension binary + SQL macros, no bundled data
themes: Country-level Airbnb studies with shared data: OECD/EU/UN reports with data appendices on platform tourism, Eurostat-Airbnb data-sharing agreement outputs, ECB/IMF papers
why_all: Repo's own environment already uses DuckDB for large-store queries; this extension would let the team pull/refresh Eurostat platform-tourism tables in the same DuckDB workflow used for Inside Airbnb, with no separate Python/R dependency.

name: us-immigration-datasets
what_it_holds: Scraper/orchestration tool (fetch_latest.py, 2,475 lines; sources.yaml defining 20+ US government sources) that pulls Visa Bulletin PDFs (FY2011-2026), Visa Statistics PDFs (2017-2025), Visa Annual Reports (FY2015-2024), LCA/H-1B and PERM labor-certification Excel files (FY2008-2026), USCIS employment forms (1991-2026), and NIV (non-immigrant visa) statistics (2021-2024) -- ~4.9GB across 1,033+ files when run. No data committed to the repo itself; public-domain/CC0 sources. Last snapshot noted 2026-03-10.
why_useful: A one-command puller for long-run US work/seasonal-visa volumes (H-1B, H-2B via LCA/PERM lineage, NIV stats) and visa-bulletin backlogs -- a proxy for foreign-worker and long-stay travel volume into the US that could feed a labor-mobility/long-stay-rental demand variable (gaps 16 and 2/3 adjacent); the NIV and Visa Bulletin PDFs may also carry seasonal (H-2B/H-2A) visa issuance figures worth extracting.
size_hint: ~4.9GB / 1,033+ files once pulled; repo itself is code-only
license: Public domain / CC0 for the tool; underlying US government sources are public domain
themes: Student, seasonal-worker, medical and other niche travel-demand datasets; university calendars; military moves
why_all: A one-command puller for long-run US work/seasonal-visa volumes (H-1B, H-2B via LCA/PERM lineage, NIV stats) and visa-bulletin backlogs -- a proxy for foreign-worker and long-stay travel volume into the US that could feed a labor-mobility/long-stay-rental demand variable (gaps 16 and 2/3 adjacent); the NIV and Visa Bulletin PDFs may also carry seasonal (H-2B/H-2A) visa issuance figures worth extracting.

name: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce public dataset (source repo)
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed repo (the original source behind the well-known Kaggle "Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist") holding sample relational tables extracted from Olist's real marketplace: orders, order items/prices, freight value, products, sellers (9,000+), customers, and reviews, covering hundreds of thousands of orders across Brazil; includes an ER-diagram schema.
why_useful: A real (not synthetic) multi-table ecommerce marketplace transaction dataset with prices, freight/shipping cost, seller counts, delivery times and customer reviews by Brazilian region — useful as a structural template for how a two-sided marketplace's take-rate/logistics-cost/review data can be organized, and as a LatAm regional ecommerce-activity dataset in its own right (LatAm demand is gap #7).
time_coverage: 2016-2018 order history (per the well-known Kaggle companion release; exact span not restated on this page)
license: MIT (repo); Kaggle release under CC BY-NC-SA
last_activity: not shown; used as a stable hiring-assessment reference dataset
size_hint: hundreds of thousands of orders, 950,000+ products, 9,000+ sellers per repo description
themes: Retail and ecommerce alt-data open samples (web-scraped prices, Amazon rank), as templates for platform KPI nowcasting
why_all: A real (not synthetic) multi-table ecommerce marketplace transaction dataset with prices, freight/shipping cost, seller counts, delivery times and customer reviews by Brazilian region — useful as a structural template for how a two-sided marketplace's take-rate/logistics-cost/review data can be organized, and as a LatAm regional ecommerce-activity dataset in its own right (LatAm demand is gap #7).

name: india-district-nightlights-viirs
what_it_holds: Committed derived-statistics panel at output/csv/nightlights_district_panel.csv: 641 Indian districts x 13 years (2012-2024) = 8,333 rows, with mean/median/sum radiance, std dev, min/max, valid-pixel counts, and log-transformed variants per district-year; also year-wise GeoJSON with district polygons. Raw VIIRS rasters are gitignored (must be re-pulled via Google Earth Engine), but the derived panel itself is committed.
why_useful: A ready-made district-level economic-activity proxy for India, one of ABNB's under-covered APAC growth markets (gap #7, regional travel volume outside US/EU) — could be aggregated to tourism-heavy districts (Goa, Kerala backwaters, Rajasthan) as an occupancy/demand proxy where no official monthly tourism series exists.
themes: Occupancy/demand estimation from satellite, nightlights, or imagery; parking-lot counts; Sentinel-based tourism activity
why_all: A ready-made district-level economic-activity proxy for India, one of ABNB's under-covered APAC growth markets (gap #7, regional travel volume outside US/EU) — could be aggregated to tourism-heavy districts (Goa, Kerala backwaters, Rajasthan) as an occupancy/demand proxy where no official monthly tourism series exists.

name: AceBee007/minpaku-reporter
what_it_holds: A Python (Poetry, pyenv, Selenium/Chromium webdriver) automation tool described as automating report work on minpaku.mlit.go.jp — Japan's official national minpaku (private lodging) registration and business-report portal run by MLIT. No committed data; it is a browser-automation client against the government's own STR reporting site, not airbnb.com.
why_useful: minpaku.mlit.go.jp is the authoritative Japanese government minpaku registration/business-days-reported system (the official counterpart to Tokyo/Kyoto minpaku registration counts). A tool that already knows how to interact with this specific official portal is a lead for automating a point-in-time pull of Japan's official minpaku registration/operating-days data, which is otherwise not on Inside Airbnb.
size_hint: small Python codebase, no data files
themes: APAC STR datasets: Tokyo/Kyoto minpaku registration data, Seoul, Bangkok, Bali, Sydney/Melbourne, Auckland, Singapore, Hong Kong Airbnb data and regulation
why_all: minpaku.mlit.go.jp is the authoritative Japanese government minpaku registration/business-days-reported system (the official counterpart to Tokyo/Kyoto minpaku registration counts). A tool that already knows how to interact with this specific official portal is a lead for automating a point-in-time pull of Japan's official minpaku registration/operating-days data, which is otherwise not on Inside Airbnb.

Confirms minpaku.mlit.go.jp is the official Japanese minpaku registration/reporting system and shows the portal's automatable workflow, but this specific tool submits a single host's own data rather than extracting aggregate registration counts — not directly a data source for gap #12/APAC regulation, only a pointer to where such data technically lives (behind login, individual-host-scoped).
